modern-new-technique-cuisine.verdict: Three named masters running three labs you can enrol in — the strongest teaching on this map that belongs to no ground at all, which is the whole point of a toolkit

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Yes in three of the four places, each a named living person teaching in their own lab: Martin Lippo at Vakuum in Barcelona, Éric Briffard at Le Cordon Bleu Paris, Miguel Ángel Cepeda in Puebla and Mexico City. Three out of four is still more than anything else on this map manages. The fourth has changed shape rather than closed: Sous Vide Australia's site now offers bespoke training built for a venue's own team, not the public workshops this map listed, and its card says so. ⛔ Where we stand: EducatedTraveler ran a paid week with Martin Lippo in October 2026, so we are not a neutral party about him. Nobody pays to be on this map and no money reaches us from him; the way in without us is his own site, martinlippo.com.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Open, and unusually so for the avant-garde. This is the rare corner of modernist cooking you can enrol in rather than apply for a stage at: private courses at Vakuum (his classroom courses for 2026 are sold out and no later date is shown, read 4 November 2026), a four-day 31-hour Advanced Culinary Techniques course in Paris taught with English translation as it is given, a multi-week diplomado in Mexico. Melbourne is no longer one of them: what is offered there is training a venue books for its own team. And the hands can ruin it — a spherification bath and liquid nitrogen are unforgiving, which is why the labs are labs.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: Yes, on the Paris course and the diplomado, which run as classes rather than as private hire. At Vakuum the way in is now a private course. What is not published anywhere is the group size at any of the four, and in a technique lab that is the number that decides whether you touch the equipment or watch it. Ask before you book.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: No, and it is worth saying why rather than treating it as a hole. The test this question applies is whether the craft, taught this way, would make sense anywhere else — and a technique toolkit is designed to travel. Sous-vide was worked out at Troisgros in 1974 and now belongs to every kitchen with a circulator. Catalonia's claim on the avant-garde is real and it is graded on this map's modernist Spanish cuisine page, where the restaurants are. Here you are buying a technique, and the technique is portable by design.

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: Nobody of ours has been, and this craft has no ladder to point at instead: its own record says there is no single formal body and that the qualification is a certificate of attendance. That is not a criticism of the labs, which are teaching real skills. It does mean that what happens after the course is entirely up to you and your own kitchen.

modern-new-technique-cuisine.ceilingNote: Four is the ceiling here, not five: the fourth answer is a settled no, because this is a toolkit rather than a tradition, and portability is what makes it worth learning.
